::: {#exm-ar1-chain}
#### A first-order autoregressive chain

Let $\arcoef$ and $\sigma > 0$ be constants,
let $\eps^{(2)}, \eps^{(3)}, \ldots \siid \ndist{0, \sigma^2}$,
and let the starting value $\param^{(1)}$ be independent of them.
For each $t \ge 1$, let

$$
\param^{(t+1)} \eqdef \arcoef\, \param^{(t)} + \eps^{(t+1)}.
$$ {#eq-ar1-chain-exm}

The sequence $\param^{(1)}, \param^{(2)}, \ldots$ is a
**first-order autoregressive** process.
Each of $\param^{(1)}, \ldots, \param^{(t)}$ is a function of
$\param^{(1)}, \eps^{(2)}, \ldots, \eps^{(t)}$,
so $\eps^{(t+1)}$ is independent of all of them.
So, given $\param^{(t)} = s$ and any earlier values,
$\param^{(t+1)} = \arcoef\, s + \eps^{(t+1)}$
has the $\ndist{\arcoef\, s, \sigma^2}$ distribution,
which depends only on the current state $s$.
The sequence is therefore a [Markov chain](#def-markov-chain).
Unlike the chain of @exm-two-state-chain,
its states can be any real number,
as are the states of the chains that MCMC builds for a continuous parameter.
:::
